speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the information. To better understand your condition, please describe the specific nature of the pain and swelling in your right knee, and when these symptoms first appeared.

Additionally, could you clarify the relationship between your knee issues and the episodes of pain during urination?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis (formerly Reiter's syndrome). The clinical picture of an asymmetric oligoarthritis (knee, ankle), urethritis (pain with urination), and a sexually active history in a young male is classic for this condition, often triggered by an STI like Chlamydia trachomatis.
